thread:
mira: Heads-up: profiler picked up a TTFT spike on /v1/chat/generate after the kernel-selector rollout this morning (cost_aware=true). I plotted a token-level waterfall and kernel time is dominating, but KV lookup time also ticked up.
mira: sample aggregated logs:
```
[2355432100] route=/v1/chat/generate token=1 ttft=123ms decode=30ms kernel=85ms kv_lookup=8ms
[2355432103] route=/v1/chat/generate token=2 ttft=200ms decode=40ms kernel=140ms kv_lookup=18ms
[2355432106] route=/v1/chat/generate token=3 ttft=95ms decode=28ms kernel=60ms kv_lookup=7ms
```
oliver: Interesting — do we know what kernel variant the selector picked for those traces? If it switched to the small-batch fused kernel that could explain kernel growth but not necessarily kv.
mira: It flipped to the cost_aware heuristic and prefers fused-kernel-x for batch targets ~=512. KV hit ratio dropped ~5% for that route in same window (dashboard). My hunch: prefetch/path handshake got delayed and KV misses are queuing.
sam: I wonder if we're mis-attributing prefetch time into kernel due to the handoff. We should split timestamps: prequeue vs kernel_enqueue vs kernel_start to see wall-time boundaries.
jia: Agreed. Should add micro-timestamps: prequeue_enter, prequeue_exit, kernel_enqueue, kernel_start, kv_start, kv_end, decode_start, decode_end. Sampling 1/100 requests should be enough to spot patterns.
mira: :thumbsup: Also want per-route percentile panels (p50/p95/p99) and stacked bars for token-level TTFT breakdown (prequeue | kernel | kv | decode | post). I'll open a Grafana ticket.
dev-bot: deploy-bot: runtime:cost_aware_kernel rolled to prod @ 2355432000 — 5 nodes
oliver: Another angle: cost_aware sometimes increases waiting to reach a kernel sweet spot (larger microbatches). If KV misses happen, that waiting becomes wasted latency and spikes TTFT.
sam: For quick triage someone run: `perf/profiler/sample --route /v1/chat/generate --since 2355432000 --limit 200` and paste top traces. We need stack-level timing.
mira: profiler sample output (top trace):
```
trace_id=abc123 start=2355432101
prequeue_enter=2355432101.000
prequeue_exit=2355432101.012
kernel_enqueue=2355432101.019
kernel_start=2355432101.020
kv_start=2355432101.080
kv_end=2355432101.095
decode_start=2355432101.100
decode_end=2355432101.130
end=2355432101.133
// ttft approx = 133ms, kernel window includes wait for kv_start in these traces
```
jia: I'll wire the micro-timestamps into the runtime sampler and add a dashboard panel that computes token-level stacked bars and per-route percentiles. Will sample at 1% for the next hour then adjust.
mira: Can we mark the rollout as suspect and consider rollback if p99 > 300ms sustained? We should also run a quick canary to compare old selector vs cost_aware on a subset of traffic.
oliver: Agreed. @eng-runtime-oncall please monitor alerts for /v1/chat/generate p99. I'll prepare a canary patch to restore old selector behavior for 10% of traffic.
sam: I'll run the profiler sampling now and push results to the incident doc. If we can reproduce locally with a test trace that triggers kv misses, we can iterate on batching heuristics.
mira: Action items: jia -> add micro-timestamps + dashboard; oliver -> canary rollback plan; sam -> profiler sampling and incident doc; mira -> compile short postmortem if rollback required. Thanks all, keep updates in this thread.
